ruling.explanation:
Both of you were at the same Tampines MRT Exit D pickup, and the trace shows it: the driver held position 24 m from the pin at 0 km/h from 18:20:00 to 18:25:30 (a single 330-second run, 30 seconds above the 300-second TRANSPORT_HUB minimum), and the rider's device sat 41.9 m from the same pin for the whole wait. On the instruments alone I accept that the four limbs of POL-NS-01 are met — the 'arrived' event is present, the first in-geofence fix precedes it, the dwell is continuous and long enough, and the trip was driver-terminated under RIDER_NO_SHOW after the clock ran out. The driver's POL-NS-02 point is also accepted (arrival inside the 150 m hub radius), as is POL-NS-05 (no false marker: 24 m from the pin and 0.0 km/h) and POL-NS-06 (no dwell shortfall: the computed figure is a 30-second surplus, not a deficit). None of that decides the case, because POL-NS-01 charges the fee only where no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it.

POL-NS-04 displaces it, on all three of its limbs. (a) The rider sent two locating/coordinating messages inside the waiting window — 18:21:00, 'I am at Exit D under the green sign. Where is your car?', naming her sub-location and asking for the driver's, and 18:23:25, 'I still cannot see you. Please reply.' (b) The driver posted no chat reply within 120 seconds of either message and placed no in-app call; the log holds only a SYSTEM notice and the rider's two messages, and in_app_calls is empty. (c) The rider's track places her within the 200 m hub presence radius on all 16 qualifying fixes, a fortiori the majority. The clause's only exits are an affirmative failure of limb (c) or a driver reply within 120 seconds; neither exists. The driver's answer — that he was physically there and waited — does not meet either exit, and the clause is written as a coordination-failure rule, not a presence rule. The driver is of course right that he served the hold, and I record that plainly; but the platform undertakes to the rider that a coordinating rider at the pin will not lose the fee to a silent driver, and that is what happened here.

Two further points. The driver's POL-NS-07 compensation claim is refused: its precondition is that POL-NS-01 stand undisplaced, and it does not, and POL-NS-04 states that no driver compensation is payable on an exoneration. The escalation request is refused: nothing in the record pits one admissible artifact against another on arrival, dwell or rider presence — the driver's written statement agrees with his own trace — so POL-NS-09(b) has nothing to bite on, and limbs (c) and (d) are negative (the same-party dispute counters are 0; no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 120 completed trips, far below the 4-and-0.08 anti-farming test). I note the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09106-01, status MISSING, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) was disclosed by the rider and does not move the arithmetic: it only makes POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation unavailable, and there is a single in-geofence interval in any event.

Result: the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full and no driver compensation is payable. Confidence is 0.90, against a cap of 1.0, because every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the chat log (the rider's messages and the driver's silence), the GPS rider track (rider presence) and the trip record (no calls) — is at full weight.
